newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate Finance chairman unveils tax cut bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate Finance chairman unveils tax cut bill.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth on Tuesday revealed his version of a net $85 billion in tax cuts over five years, including differences from a proposal in the House of Representatives.

The Delaware Republican's bill included tax initiatives for higher education that cost $32 billion over five years, a $500 child tax credit for children under age 17 and a cut in the capital gains tax rate to 20 percent from the current 28 percent maximum. It would not cut the corporate capital gains tax rate as the House legislation would.

Roth's bill is expected to be considered by the Senate Finance Committee on Thursday. The House Ways and Means Committee last Friday approved its proposal to implement the tax cuts outlined in last month's balanced budget agreement between congressional leaders and the White House.
The bill would extend the airline ticket tax, but reduce the air passenger ticket tax rate to 7.5 percent from 10 percent for certain segments and impose a fee on international departures.

It would also extend eligibility for Individual Retirement Accounts, but did not include elimination of the ethanol subsidy, which was in the House bill. It would raise the threshold at which the estate tax kicks in to $1 million from $600,000 over 11 years.

The bill includes a federal unemployment surtax that would raise $6.4 billion over five years. Eventually differences in the Senate and House bills must be worked out before the final bill could go to the White House.
